subject: Request: tiered A/B release with automatic fallback & VIP pin for Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: tiered A/B release with automatic fallback & VIP pin for Acme Analytics

Team —

Acme Analytics (PA enterprise, deal DW-ACME-2026-17) has signed and we need a deployment plan that preserves their 99.9% latency SLA during model migration. They specifically requested controlled A/B exposure to validate latency/quality on their production traffic and to allow us to test the new tokenizer/quantization changes.

Ask: approve a temporary exception to the standard canary cap so we can run a tiered A/B progression: 10% -> 25% -> 50% over ~48 hours (manual gates between steps). In parallel we must implement an automatic fallback (per-tenant pin + immediate re-route to stable model variant) if latency or error thresholds exceed safe limits. We also need audit logs for any pin/fallback events.

Why: the volatility in Acme's traffic pattern means a 5% canary won't give statistically meaningful latency signals. We have legal and CS asks to allow a VIP pin for ACME during business hours for cutover windows.

Please reply with the technical guardrails, rollback timelines, and any operational runbook items. I attached the SLA exception form — fill the technical section and return.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Attachment: sla_exception_form.docx (fillable)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: tiered A/B release with automatic fallback & VIP pin for Acme Analytics

Thanks Hannah — high level plan below. I filled the technical portion of the SLA exception form and attached the runbook (canary_runbook_v2.pdf).

Summary of controls (short):
- Canary type: A/B routing by user/tenant header (X-Redwood-Tenant) with deterministic hashing for reproducibility.
- Progression: 10% (24h) -> 25% (12h) -> 50% (12h) with manual hold at each stage and automated health checks.
- Health metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency delta vs baseline, request error rate, model-tokenization mismatch errors, acceptance rate on ACME evaluation prompts. Primary thresholds: p95 > baseline + 150ms OR error rate > 0.5% triggers automated rollback.
- Automated fallback: routing policy in control plane will shift 100% of ACME traffic to the pinned stable model variant when any threshold is breached for >60s (sliding window). Fallback timeline: detection -> 60s evaluation -> traffic shift initiated -> full reroute within target 2 minutes.
- Per-tenant pin: we will create an explicit pinning rule for ACME in the routing table (priority over global rollouts). Pin toggles require QA+PM sign-off via the console feature-flag workflow.
- Circuit breaker: if upstream GPU nodes report overload >85% or queue latency spikes, a circuit will short-circuit to the lower-capacity quantized variant or to cached responses for read-only endpoints.
- Observability: we will enable trace sampling for all canary requests, add token-level cost/latency breakdown, and stream audit events to a dedicated bucket ACL'd for Acme legal review.

Operational notes:
- Warmup: pre-warm KV cache by seeding popular prefixes for ACME (this avoids cold-start p99 spikes).
- Cache priming window: start 2 hours prior to traffic shift.
- Escalation: Pager route to on-call infra engineer, then Eng Lead.

I also created SUP-1776 to track the automation tasks (routing policy, pin UI, audit export). Link in the runbook.

Attachment: canary_runbook_v2.pdf

—Aditya
Aditya Rao
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
aditya_rao@redwood.com
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Dec 2026 13:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: tiered A/B release with automatic fallback & VIP pin for Acme Analytics

Adding the product perspective:
- I support the 10->25->50 progression but recommend we add an intermediate 25% hold of 24 hours for quality checks on hallucination/regression tests. Latency alone misses quality regressions tied to tokenizer changes.
- For business hours pin: agree that we should allow a per-tenant pin during agreed maintenance windows. Pin must be explicitly reversible by us and documented in the change record.
- SLAs/credits: we should coordinate with Legal/Finance to have a short amendment covering temporary exposure and remediation credits if fallback fails to restore SLA.

Requesting CS (Monica) to confirm whether Acme will accept staged exposure and whether they require a separate rollback clause in their order form.

Laura
Laura Bennett
Product Manager, Redwood Console
laura_bennett@redwood.com
From: Maya Patel <maya@acme-analytics.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 10:22:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Request: tiered A/B release with automatic fallback & VIP pin for Acme Analytics

Thanks for the detailed plan. A couple of clarifications from Acme:
1) We want a hard pin option during our principal business hours (0900–1700 ET) so that if the canary is promoting and any issue appears, our traffic is immediately served by the pinned stable model.
2) We require an audit trail for any pin/unpin/fallback event (timestamp, initiating user, reason, pre/post metrics). Ideally pushed to our S3 bucket or available via a signed link.
3) If automatic fallback occurs and we still see SLA violations for >4 hours, we will expect either a remediation credit or an agreed remediation plan.

Please confirm these items and the expected detection->reroute time.

Best,
Maya Patel
Director of Platform, Acme Analytics
maya@acme-analytics.com
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: tiered A/B release with automatic fallback & VIP pin for Acme Analytics

Hi Maya —

We can support all three items. Quick confirmations:
- Hard pin during 09:00–17:00 ET: we will add a tenant-level pin that takes precedence over rollouts; toggling requires two approvers (CS + PM) and will be visible in the audit log.
- Audit trail: we will stream pin/fallback events to an ACL'd S3 bucket and provide signed time-limited links. The payload will include timestamp, operator, metric snapshot, and routing decision.
- SLA remediation: if automatic fallback happens and SLA violations persist >4 hours, we will escalate to the account team and coordinate remediation credits per your contract. Legal will prepare a short amendment for the maintenance window changes.

Expected detection->reroute time: Aditya estimates detection + evaluation 60s, traffic shift initiated and effective within ~2 minutes in most cases. We will capture this in the runbook and have an on-call engineer during the initial deployment window.

I'll loop Legal and Finance once Aditya posts SUP-1776 updates and runbook.

Thanks,
Hannah
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: tiered A/B release with automatic fallback & VIP pin for Acme Analytics

Quick technical follow-up and runbook pointer: SUP-1776 now contains the automation subtasks. Key points:
- Detection logic: sliding 60s window; alerts if p95 > baseline + 150ms OR error rate >0.5%. We sample traces at 100% for tenant to collect token-level stats during canary.
- Automatic reroute: implemented as a routing-policy transaction in the control plane. When threshold trips, the policy flips a per-tenant rule atomically. We then backfill cache and ramp down canary instances.
- Safety: rollback will not happen mid-request; in-flight requests will complete on the canary model; subsequent requests route to stable.
- Observability/export: weekly exports to Acme S3 + immediate event push on pin/unpin/fallback. We will provide signed URL delivery after initial test.
- Test window suggestion: schedule the 10% -> 25% progression starting Friday 17:00 ET to capture peak behavior, with full runbook dry-run 24h prior.

I'll update the runbook with explicit CLI commands and the console screenshots for the pin toggle.

—Aditya
